Hi Sandeep / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we all have the same view. I’ve copied Aditya from our infra team to confirm technical feasibility and constraints.

Recap / asks we captured:
- Primary workloads: customer-facing chat (streaming) + async batch inference for offline scoring.
- Target latency SLOs (please confirm these are the business targets):
  - US (primary): p95 end-to-end < 150ms for synchronous requests, streaming chunk latency < 100ms
  - EU: p95 end-to-end < 180ms
  - APAC: p95 end-to-end < 220ms (APAC user base is smaller but latency-sensitive)
- Throughput & concurrency: sustained 800 reqs/sec across fleet with bursts to 2k, concurrency per-customer ~500 sessions (streaming pinned per-session)
- Streaming: need token-by-token streaming to client with <100ms chunk latency and session affinity to region
- Data residency: EU customer data at rest and logs stored in EU region; APAC regulatory requirement for Japan-based/SG region for certain datasets
- Security/compliance: SOC2 + TLS in transit + customer-managed KMS for keys (if possible)

Next steps suggested:
1) Aditya to confirm multi-region routing architecture and any tradeoffs for the SLOs above (expected warm vs cold p95).
2) Redwood to provide a short PoC config (per-region capacity estimate + expected cost ballpark).
3) Schedule a 1-hour technical workshop (infra + security + Finova infra) — calendar link below.
4) I attached the quick requirements sheet we used to capture today’s numbers. Please update the EU/APAC residency lines and return.

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- The latency targets you listed are in line with our expectations; the business team would like to tighten US p95 to 120ms if possible, but we understand that’s aggressive.
- Data residency: for EU we need both data at rest and logs never to leave EU. For APAC we’d prefer SG or Tokyo depending on final compliance review — I’ll confirm which once Priya loops in our compliance lead.

2) Any constraints on streaming sessions spanning regions (e.g., client moves from EU to APAC mid-session) — does Redwood pin sessions to region?

Hi all —

Thanks for the detailed recap, Marissa, and good clarifications Sandeep. High level answers and constraints from an infra/serving POV:

Architecture & routing:
- We recommend a multi-region deployment with regional inference endpoints (US, EU, APAC). Traffic is routed to the nearest region by default (edge load-balancers) and we support sticky session routing for streaming (session affinity pinned to the region for the duration of the websocket/stream).
- Failover options:
  - Soft failover within-region to a compatible model variant (quantized or lower-capacity model) — no data residency change.
  - Cross-region failover (EU -> US) is supported but will route payloads through the target region; this would violate EU-at-rest/log residency unless you accept transient replication or we configure anonymization/filtered logging. We can discuss policy for audit.

Latency & concurrency notes:
- Warm p95 guidance (approx, depends on model & sequence length):
  - US: ~80–140ms p95 (for typical LLMs and our optimized kernels) if KV cache hits and batching tuned for latency; cold-start penalties can be several hundred ms for GPU-backed workers if model weights need to be loaded.
  - EU: add ~20–40ms network tail depending on provider region and peering
  - APAC: add ~40–80ms network tail; consider regional model edge instances to remove tail latency.
- Streaming: token-chunk latency target <100ms is achievable with pinned streaming sessions and small-chunk batching; need to tune batching threshold carefully to avoid tail latency spikes.
- Throughput & concurrency: your 800 rps sustained / bursts to 2k is feasible with autoscaling and pooling; for 500 concurrent streaming sessions we recommend provisioning a modest pool of warm workers per region and enabling continuous warm cache (reserved capacity or dedicated).

Data residency & key management:
- We can ensure data at rest is stored in-region (EU) and restrict log retention to regionally isolated buckets. For cross-region failover we can implement policy-based redaction/anonymization, but that requires agreement.
- KMS: we support provider-managed and customer-managed keys (HSM-backed KMS integrations). Customer KMS requires a short onboarding step.

Proposed PoC config (starting point):
- US region: 2 GPU workers (A100/RTX equivalent), warm pool, expected sustained throughput ~900 rps with p95 ~120ms for your model;
- EU region: 1–2 GPU workers with warm pool, p95 ~150–170ms expected;
- APAC region: 1 GPU worker, p95 ~200–240ms expected;
- Logging and audit: EU-resident S3 buckets, separate log sink in APAC where required.

Attachments: [Attachment: regional-routing-design.png (PNG)]

I’ll put together a short one-pager with expected capacity and a cost ballpark for hosted vs dedicated. If you anticipate sustained heavy load or strict compliance (full KMS + isolated tenancy), dedicated capacity is typically the cleaner option.

Happy to join the workshop; let me know available slots.

—Aditya
